Thanks Taylor — received. I'm opening intake and looping legal & sales to scope the first-pass redlines. A couple of clarifying items we need now so we can prioritize:

- Primary product: is this a hosted Redwood API deal or dedicated capacity? (affects SLA & residency answers)
- Target residency for customer data (US only / EU required / multi-region?)
- Who is the signer for Novanet? Procurement or CFO? We need signer name + email for the signature map.

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Novanet MSA + Order Form (initial)

Camila — taking this. Quick notes from a legal triage perspective:

- Liability / Cap: Novanet's MSA proposes a mutual cap at 2x fees and broad consequential exclusions. Ask: if this is Dedicated deployment, we should push for a higher cap or carveouts for data breach remediation.
- Residency: If Novanet needs EU residency, we'll need to confirm hosting region and update Exhibit B and data processing addendum.
- Audit / SOC2: procurement asked for evidence; we should attach our SOC 2 summary and a statement about audit access limitations.
- Indemnities: redline will propose clarifications around 3rd-party IP claims and limits tied to misuse vs. platform defects.

I'll prepare a marked-up MSA with color-coded severity (Blocker / Major / Minor) and circulate to sales by EOD Thursday (48 hours). If procurement expects Dec 10 signature, we should lock commercial terms (price, term, seat counts) this week; legal can accelerate once commercial is stable.

Jonas — can you confirm whether platform residency options include EU for Novanet? If not, we should flag multi-region gating.

— Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

On pricing / timeline: we can target Dec 10 signature if (a) legal completes redlines by Nov 20 and (b) procurement confirms order form details (term, seats). I can approve standard PLG discounts; anything outside standard playbook will need commercial manager approval.

Camila — please use "intake-checklist.pdf" template and add seat counts + pilot SLOs. Kim — if you need a higher cap for Hosted, we may suggest a price-protected uplift instead of extensive negotiation.
